why_unapproved: SPEAK-EVAL-010 depends on 'enough double-rated data and stable pipeline'.
Neither exists yet. No item in the dataset has two independent human ratings,
so human-human agreement has never been measured -- and section 11.4 of the
plan is explicit that numeric floors must be chosen after that measurement,
and that the generic 80% accuracy rule is not evidence-based and must not be
The thresholds below are therefore PROVISIONAL and carry no empirical
rationale. `approved: false` makes the gate refuse to enforce them: a release
decision made against invented numbers is worse than no automated decision,
To approve: measure human-human agreement on a double-rated calibration set,
replace the values below with ones derived from it, record the derivation in
`rationale`, and have the assessment and product owners set `approved: true`
with their names. That is a reviewable change to this file, which is the
point -- see `gate.py` on why a threshold cannot be set from inside a run.

absolute._note: Floors a candidate must clear on its own, regardless of history.

min_within_half_band.suggestion_basis: Placeholder. Must be set at or below observed qualified-rater reliability, which has not been measured.

max_mae.suggestion_basis: Placeholder. Half a band is one step of the scale; two steps is plainly unusable. The defensible line between them is an empirical question.

max_abs_bias.suggestion_basis: Placeholder. Bias is the recalibratable component, so its ceiling is a product decision about how wrong a systematic offset may be.

min_coverage.suggestion_basis: Placeholder. Proportion of items that produced a valid score.

non_regression._note: A candidate must not be materially worse than the current baseline, even if it clears the absolute floors.
non_regression._paired_note: Item-level paired bootstrap, not a comparison of two independent means. The items are the same and their difficulty is shared; discarding that widens the interval for no reason and reports a real regression as inconclusive.

slices._note: A metric over a slice too small to be stable is noise presented as a finding.

bias_escalation._note: Bias by slice is a fairness question, not a quality one, and it escalates to a person rather than failing a build.
bias_escalation._escalation_note: Set false deliberately. An automated fairness gate on unapproved thresholds would either block everything or nothing, and both teach people to ignore it. It raises a review instead.

sample_size._note: Below this, a gate decision is not supportable at all and the gate abstains rather than guessing.
